papers.title: EvoAD: Self-Evolving Autonomous Driving via Latent World-Model Guided Post-hoc Reflection
papers.authors_text: Junjie Yang, Qiming Zhang, Yuyan Li, Shuqi Shen, Yusong Huang, Yanggang Sheng, Wenpeng Xu, Ziyi Shi, Tianshun Li, Yijie Chen, Yujia Wang, Jun Ma, Xinhu Zheng, Hongliang Lu, Hai Yang
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving systems have achieved rapid progress by learning unified policies that map sensor observations directly to driving trajectories. However, once deployed, these systems typically remain frozen: they may repeat similar decisions in similar scenes, and failures can only be addressed through costly data collection and retraining. This sharply contrasts with human drivers, who improve lifelong through experience, memory, and reflection. In this work, we ask whether autonomous driving systems can achieve similar post-deployment self-evolution to human drivers. We propose EvoAD, a self-evolving autonomous driving framework via latent world-model guided post-hoc reflection. EvoAD stores driving experiences in a bird's-eye-view feature memory pool, retrieves scene-relevant precedents according to geometric and semantic similarity, and uses a latent world model to evaluate the future consequences of candidate trajectories in a compact planning-oriented space. Instead of treating memory as external textual contexts or using world models only for pre-action simulation, EvoAD transforms executed driving outcomes into reusable improvement signals for future decisions. This enables the system to diagnose how prior trajectories could have been improved and to refine behavior in similar future scenarios without retraining the base driving policy. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 and v2 show consistent improvements across reflection rounds and state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating the potential of world models as reflective mechanisms for post-deployment self-evolution in autonomous driving.
papers.tldr: EvoAD enables post-deployment self-evolution of autonomous driving policies by storing BEV driving experiences, retrieving similar precedents, and using a latent world model to reflect on executed trajectories and refine future decisions without retraining, achieving state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM.

detailed_reading.motivation: 端到端自动驾驶策略部署后通常保持冻结，容易在相似场景重复相似决策，失败只能依赖昂贵的数据采集与重训练来修正，缺乏人类驾驶员通过经验、记忆和反思实现终身改进的能力。论文因此提出后部署自演化问题：能否在不重训练基础驾驶策略的前提下，让系统利用已执行经验持续诊断并改进未来决策。
detailed_reading.method: EvoAD将驾驶经验存入鸟瞰图特征记忆池，依据几何与语义相似度检索与当前场景相关的前例，并利用潜在世界模型在面向规划的紧凑空间中评估候选轨迹的未来后果。系统把已执行驾驶结果转化为可复用的改进信号，通过事后反思诊断先前轨迹可改进之处，并在相似未来场景中细化行为；基础驾驶策略保持冻结，不进行重训练。
detailed_reading.result: 在NAVSIM v1和v2上的实验显示，EvoAD随反思轮次增加取得一致性能提升，并达到当前最优性能。结果支持将世界模型作为反思机制，使端到端自动驾驶系统在部署后利用经验记忆实现自演化，而无需重新训练基础策略。
detailed_reading.conclusion: EvoAD表明，基于潜在世界模型引导的事后反思与BEV经验记忆，可以为自动驾驶系统提供部署后的持续改进路径。其核心价值在于把记忆从外部文本上下文转变为可复用改进信号，并把世界模型从仅用于行动前模拟扩展为行动后反思与策略细化机制。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括BEV特征记忆池、基于几何与语义相似度的场景前例检索、规划导向紧凑空间中的潜在世界模型后果评估，以及将执行结果回写为反思信号的事后改进闭环；基础策略冻结以控制部署后更新成本。局限在于摘要未给出记忆容量、检索阈值、世界模型训练细节、反思轮次与具体指标数值，且验证局限于NAVSIM v1/v2，真实部署中的记忆漂移、世界模型偏差与在线安全约束仍需进一步评估。

papers.title: Adaptive Rejection of Unknown Hybrid Sinusoidal Disturbances with Application to Humanoid Walking under Unknown Ground Motion
papers.authors_text: I-Chia Chang, Jacob Stewart, Petros A. Ioannou, Yan Gu
papers.abstract: Legged robot control is not yet practical in non-inertial environments, where the ground and surroundings accelerate in the inertial Earth frame, mainly because of the unknown, time-varying, persistent perturbations caused by environmental motion, compounded by the associated hybrid robotic dynamics. We formulate the problem of robot walking control as unknown-disturbance rejection for hybrid linear systems subject to hybrid sinusoidal disturbances (i.e., a linear combination of sinusoidal components with instantaneous phase jumps at discrete events). First, necessary and sufficient conditions for solvability of the disturbance rejection problem are derived and used to characterize the control input that rejects the disturbances. Second, with the Youla-Kucera parametrization, an output feedback controller capable of rejecting the disturbance is introduced. Third, an adaptive law is proposed to estimate the controller parameters that reject the disturbance in the practical case where the disturbance and its parameters are unknown. Experiments on bipedal walking during ground motion demonstrate substantially improved body-position tracking accuracy, with an average improvement of over 60% in simulations and up to 47% in real-world experiments.
papers.tldr: This paper develops an adaptive output-feedback controller that rejects unknown hybrid sinusoidal disturbances in hybrid linear systems and demonstrates its effectiveness for bipedal walking under unknown ground motion, substantially improving body-position tracking accuracy in simulation and real-world experiments.

detailed_reading.motivation: 非惯性环境中地面与周围环境在惯性系中加速，会给双腿机器人带来未知、时变且持续的扰动，并与支撑脚切换等混合动力学耦合，使现有数据驱动方法缺乏理论保证、反馈/预测控制又常假设地面运动已知或将扰动简化为有界输入。本文因此直接把机器人行走控制建模为受混合正弦扰动作用的混合线性系统未知扰动抑制问题，以面向未知地面运动下的双足行走。
detailed_reading.method: 论文将系统写成含连续相位微分动力学和离散事件跳变的混合线性系统，并把扰动建模为若干正弦分量叠加且在每个离散事件处发生瞬时相位跳变；先推导混合调节器方程，给出扰动抑制可解的充要条件及理想部分状态反馈控制输入，再基于Youla-Kucera参数化构造输出反馈控制器，并通过混合结构抵消跳变带来的时变过渡效应；在扰动状态和参数未知时，提出自适应律并借助混合交换引理得到线性参数估计方程，在线估计补偿器参数。最后将该混合自适应控制器嵌入双足机器人分层控制框架，用于未知多方向运动平台上的行走。
detailed_reading.result: 理论结果给出了混合线性系统抑制混合正弦扰动的充要可解条件，并证明所设计的自适应输出反馈控制器可在扰动及参数未知时实现输出收敛。实验在MuJoCo高保真仿真和Digit机器人真实平台行走中验证，未知多方向地面运动下质心位置跟踪误差平均降低超过60%（仿真），真实实验最高降低47%，表明无需完整地面运动知识也能显著改善跟踪精度。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 该工作将非惯性环境双足行走控制提升为混合线性系统的未知混合正弦扰动抑制问题，提供了从可解性条件、输出反馈控制器到自适应参数估计的完整框架，并在仿真与硬件上验证了有效性。结果表明混合自适应输出反馈控制可在未知、时变、持续地面扰动下提升双足机器人质心跟踪，为混合动力学机器人在非惯性环境中的控制提供了有理论保证的路径。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键假设包括离散事件周期T恒定、无扰动系统稳定、连续扰动谱与系统谱不相交，理论分析阶段已知系统与扰动矩阵，实际控制仅用测量输出且不依赖扰动状态和特征；扰动先验为有限个正弦分量叠加并在离散事件处相位跳变，控制器参数在线自适应且Youla-Kucera结构用于维持闭环稳定性，混合交换引理把参数估计转化为线性方程。局限在于采用降阶混合线性模型和正弦扰动先验，可能难以覆盖强非线性、非平稳或复杂碰撞主导的地面运动，验证场景也局限于特定双足平台与实验条件。

papers.title: A Heterogeneous UAV UGV Methodology for Aerial Tracking of Mini Autonomous Cars
papers.authors_text: Santiago Fernandez, Angel da Silva, Hiago Sodre, Pablo Moraes, Bruna Gutterres, Ricardo B. Grando
papers.abstract: Aerial tracking of autonomous ground vehicles can provide useful situational awareness in environments where fixed external perception infrastructure is unavailable. However, visual-only tracking from an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is limited by camera field of view, viewpoint changes, occlusions, and temporary loss of target visibility. This paper presents a heterogeneous UAV--UGV methodology for aerial tracking of small-scale autonomous ground vehicles in simulation. The system is implemented in ROS~2 and Gazebo Sim using a Tello-like UAV equipped with a front-facing RGB camera and multiple LIMO-like unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). Three approaches are evaluated: a training-free color-marker baseline, a YOLO-based visual baseline, and a proposed UAV--UGV fusion method. The proposed method uses the same visual detector as the YOLO baseline, but combines visual detections with UGV state information to maintain the target estimate during visual gaps. The methods are evaluated across four scenarios: single-car tracking, crossing trajectories, occlusion, and UAV-assisted awareness. Results over 600 simulation runs show that the proposed fusion method achieves nearly continuous track coverage across all scenarios while reducing localization error relative to the YOLO baseline. Compared with the visual-only YOLO approach, the fusion method reduces RMSE by 37.3\%, 64.2\%, 62.6\%, and 61.8\% in the four evaluated scenarios, respectively. The method also enables conflict-awareness lead times of 10.20~s in the crossing scenario and 9.07~s in the UAV-assisted awareness scenario. These results indicate that heterogeneous UAV--UGV fusion can improve aerial tracking continuity and robustness when visual observations are intermittent.
papers.tldr: This paper presents a ROS 2/Gazebo Sim heterogeneous UAV–UGV framework that fuses YOLO-based aerial detections with UGV state information to maintain continuous tracking of mini autonomous cars during visual gaps, achieving near-continuous coverage and substantially lower localization error than visual-only YOLO tracking.

detailed_reading.motivation: 无人机对地面自主车辆的空中跟踪可在缺乏固定外部感知基础设施时提供态势感知，但纯视觉跟踪受相机视场、视角变化、遮挡和目标暂时不可见限制。异质UAV-UGV系统具有互补能力：UAV提供高位广域视角，UGV提供稳定地面状态信息，因此需要评估共享UGV状态信息能否在视觉中断时保持空中跟踪连续性。
detailed_reading.method: 在ROS 2 Jazzy与Gazebo Sim中构建Tello类UAV（前视RGB相机）和LIMO类UGV的仿真系统，场景控制器生成四类运动轨迹，视觉检测器处理UAV图像，跟踪模块将检测转换为目标状态，评估器记录覆盖率和定位误差。对比三种方法：无训练颜色标记基线采用RGB阈值与连通域滤波；YOLOv8视觉基线用仿真图像训练，标签由RGB图像中可见标记生成，并以检测框和前视相机测距模型估计目标位置；提出的UAV-UGV融合法使用同一YOLOv8检测器，有检测时用视觉量测更新目标状态，无检测时用UGV共享的位置、姿态和速度信息进行状态预测以维持目标估计。每个场景采用5个随机种子、每种子10次试验，每种方法共200次运行、每场景50次。
detailed_reading.result: 600次仿真中三种方法各完成200次有效运行，未出现假阳性、ID切换或YOLO检测器回退。融合法在所有场景取得最低RMSE和最高跟踪覆盖率，相较YOLO视觉基线在S1至S4的RMSE分别降低37.3%、64.2%、62.6%和61.8%，跟踪覆盖率分别提升36.7、64.5、61.7和65.1个百分点；冲突预警提前量在交叉场景为10.20 s、UAV辅助感知场景为9.07 s。颜色基线定位误差较高，YOLO基线在目标可见时定位准确但视觉缺失时跟踪中断。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 结果表明，异质UAV-UGV融合能在视觉观测间歇时维持目标估计，显著提高空中跟踪连续性和鲁棒性，并支持交叉与共享区域场景的冲突预警。由于融合法与YOLO基线共用同一检测器，其性能增益可归因于UGV状态信息的引入而非更强视觉检测器。该方法适用于无固定感知基础设施下的车队监控与地面感知辅助，但当前证据限于仿真小尺度场景。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现点包括：颜色基线无需训练但易受视角、光照、标记可见性和几何投影误差影响；YOLO标签从RGB可见标记生成以避免前视相机几何投影造成错误标签，检测结果通过边界框测距模型转换为位置；融合法不引入额外学习损失或复杂超参，核心是根据视觉检测可用性在视觉更新与UGV状态预测之间切换；评价指标含检测覆盖率、跟踪覆盖率、RMSE、MAE、位置标准差、假阳性、ID切换和冲突提前量；局限为仅仿真验证、小尺度车辆、预定义轨迹，并假设UGV状态可共享且未充分建模通信延迟与状态不确定性。

papers.title: DUET: Decoupled Upper- and Lower-Body Execution for Task-Agnostic Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors_text: Kapalik Khanal, Biswash Khatiwada, Stephen Afrifa, Fan Wu, Ramesh Bahadur Bist
papers.abstract: Changing a humanoid robot's manipulation policy should not require retraining the controller that maintains the robot's balance. This study introduces DUET, a decoupled execution framework that enables locomotion and manipulation controllers to operate simultaneously by combining their commands only at the robot interface. A reinforcement-learning locomotion policy controls the 12 leg joints and a waist yaw joint, tracking planar velocity, turning rate, and pelvis height from deep crouching to upright standing on a 23-degree-of-freedom Unitree G1. The 10 arm joints are excluded from the action space, while their positions and velocities are included only as observations, so that any compatible manipulation policy that generates arm-joint targets can control the upper body, and the locomotion policy keeps the lower body stable without requiring shared training or direct coordination. This study demonstrates the modular approach on hardware by pairing the same locomotion checkpoint with two different vision-language-action models, GR00T N1.7 and pi0.5. In simulation evaluation, the locomotion controller kept the robot's lower body stable with no falls while tracking the commanded planar velocity, yaw rate, and pelvis height with errors of 0.186 m/s, 0.142 rad/s, and 0.016 m, respectively. Ablation studies identify the upper-body pose curriculum as the dominant component, and removing this training step reduces episode survival from 20.0 to 7.4 seconds and increases the fall rate to 6.06 per environment minute. Robustness tests show no falls under pushes of up to 1.0 m/s within the trained payload range, and no falls at twice the payload limit for pushes below 0.7 m/s. These results show that a manipulation policy can be exchanged without retraining, restarting, or otherwise touching the layer that keeps the robot upright.
papers.tldr: DUET is a decoupled humanoid loco-manipulation framework in which a reinforcement-learning lower-body controller stabilizes and moves a Unitree G1 while treating the arms only as observations, allowing interchangeable manipulation policies such as vision-language-action models to control the upper body without retraining or modifying the balance controller.

detailed_reading.motivation: 人形机器人常把移动与操作分开开发，但现有整身策略或显式协调方案会把操作策略与维持平衡的控制器耦合，导致更换操作任务或策略时需要联合训练、适配甚至重训。作者希望把下肢稳定做成可复用的移动层，使任意兼容的操作策略都能在不触碰运动控制器的前提下驱动上身。
detailed_reading.method: DUET在23自由度Unitree G1上运行两个独立进程：RL运动策略以50 Hz控制12个腿关节和1个腰偏航关节，输出相对于标称姿态的13维关节位置偏移，由200 Hz关节PD跟踪；10个手臂关节不进入动作空间，仅以位置和速度作为71维观测的一部分。运动策略跟踪平面速度、偏航率和骨盆高度命令，高度范围0.18至0.73 m，移动时限制在0.60 m以上，并用20项奖励、上身姿态课程、镜像对称增强和域随机化在MuJoCo并行仿真中训练后导出为自描述ONNX。部署时两个进程通过DDS通信，运动进程是底层命令话题的唯一写入者，每周期从单独的手臂话题复制最近的手臂目标与增益，操作策略约15 Hz发布动作块，运动进程在间隔内保持上一目标，因此手臂策略可替换且其停顿不会阻塞腿部。
detailed_reading.result: 仿真中运动控制器无跌倒，平面速度、偏航率和骨盆高度跟踪误差分别为0.186 m/s、0.142 rad/s和0.016 m；消融显示上身姿态课程贡献最大，移除后回合存活时间从20.0 s降至7.4 s，跌倒率升至每环境分钟6.06次。鲁棒性测试中，在训练负载范围内承受最高1.0 m/s推力无跌倒，在2倍负载上限下低于0.7 m/s推力仍无跌倒；硬件上同一运动检查点成功配对了GR00T N1.7和pi0.5两个VLA。
detailed_reading.conclusion: DUET证明下肢稳定层可以与上身操作策略解耦，操作策略的更换无需重训、重启或修改维持平衡的控制器，从而把人形机器人下肢变成可复用的移动能力层。该设计以放弃部分整身协调和手臂作为动量执行器的能力为代价，换取操作模型的可插拔性。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括：动作仅覆盖13个下肢关节，手臂状态仅作观测；观测含基座角速度、投影重力、速度命令、步态相位、23关节位置速度、上一动作和骨盆高度命令；奖励含速度、偏航率、高度跟踪及姿态、步态、关节限位、动作平滑和终止惩罚，终止权重为-200；训练采用上身六类锚点姿态课程、镜像数据增强与镜像一致性惩罚、域随机化。约束与局限包括手臂目标以限速方式原样透传、深蹲仅限静止命令、移动时高度不低于0.60 m，且解耦相对整身控制存在姿态代价，硬件验证主要是同一运动检查点搭配两个VLA的模块化演示。

papers.title: From Likelihood to Utility: Quality-Axis Diffusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors_text: Junjie Yang, Ziyi Shi, Shuqi Shen, Xinhu Zheng, Hongliang Lu, Hai Yang
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have become a dominant paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet existing planners organize trajectory generation along the Gaussian-noise axis, treating driving utility only as an auxiliary guidance or selection signal. We instead formulate diffusion along a driving-quality axis. We propose QualiDrive, which constructs scene-specific quality ladders by ranking observed trajectories according to measured driving utility and learns to reverse this ordered degradation through ordered low-to-high-quality refinement. Each reverse step is conditioned on the scene, ego state, current trajectory, and target quality level, progressively refining trajectories toward higher driving quality. On NAVSIM, QualiDrive achieves 94.5 PDMS on v1 and a state-of-the-art 92.74 EPDMS on v2. QualiDrive improves Oracle EPDMS only modestly over endpoint-only quality supervision (98.52 to 98.57), but substantially increases the fractions of candidates above 0.95 and 0.98 EPDMS from 12.94%/9.71% to 21.53%/15.93%, raising selected EPDMS from 92.63 to 92.74. These results suggest that diffusion is not merely a process of denoising, but one of progressive quality-ordered refinement.
papers.tldr: QualiDrive reframes diffusion for end-to-end autonomous driving along a driving-quality axis—using scene-specific quality ladders and quality-conditioned low-to-high refinement—rather than Gaussian noise, yielding state-of-the-art NAVSIM performance by directly generating higher-utility trajectories.

detailed_reading.motivation: 现有端到端扩散规划器沿高斯噪声轴组织轨迹生成，把驾驶效用仅作为辅助引导或候选选择信号，导致生成过程追求人类示范分布下的高似然，而非安全、进度、舒适等多目标下的高驾驶效用。论文提出将扩散坐标从噪声水平改为驾驶质量，以直接对齐规划目标。
detailed_reading.method: QualiDrive先用大规模场景-轨迹评分库对同一意图下的观测轨迹按驾驶效用排序，构建场景特定的六级质量阶梯，并学习从低质量到高质量的有序反向细化。每个反向步骤以场景图像、自车状态、当前轨迹以及当前和目标质量等级为条件，通过DINOv2场景编码器与轨迹编码器交叉注意力融合，残差式预测下一级更高质轨迹；前向过程为高质量到低质量的有序退化并叠加小幅高斯扰动，反向过程执行五次确定性质量跃迁。训练损失包含逐级轨迹回归与平滑、质量分数回归、单调改进排序损失和终点回归；推理时生成512个候选，再由预测九项场景条件子分数的多目标评分器排序选最优轨迹。
detailed_reading.result: 在NAVSIM上，QualiDrive在v1取得94.5 PDMS，在v2取得92.74 EPDMS，较此前最佳提升2.34分。相较仅端点质量监督，Oracle EPDMS仅从98.52小幅升至98.57，但EPDMS高于0.95和0.98的候选比例从12.94%/9.71%提升至21.53%/15.93%，使选中EPDMS从92.63升至92.74。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 结果表明扩散规划不必只是去噪或恢复示范轨迹，而可以沿可测驾驶质量轴进行渐进式质量有序细化，从提升似然转向提升效用。该质量轴扩散框架在提升候选池高质量密度与最终选择性能上均有效，并在NAVSIM v1/v2达到领先结果。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括262144条有效轨迹在103288个训练场景上的评分库，约270亿场景-轨迹标签；质量阶梯按意图和路径原型分组，六级节点均为真实观测轨迹而非插值，目标质量按线性间隔选取并允许非回退，共享质量调度为q=(0,0.28,0.50,0.67,0.88,1)，相对进度计算使用epsilon=1e-4。生成器采用逐级轨迹回归、平滑、质量回归、相邻级单调排序铰链损失和终点回归，评分器用掩码二元交叉熵训练九个子分数并按NC、DAC、DDC、TL及TTC、EP、LK、HC、EC加权组合。推理时仅在初始低质量状态注入随机性，级间不再加噪，评分器独立于生成器且不访问评测器输出；评分库与阶梯仅用于训练，方法仍受有限轨迹库和评测质量函数依赖约束。

papers.title: ContactKernels: Adaptive Proposals using Geometry-COnditioned Wrenches for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.authors_text: Aditya Kamireddypalli, Matías Mattamala, João Moura, Sethu Vijayakumar, Steve Tonneau, Subramanian Ramamoorthy
papers.abstract: Contact-rich insertion requires precise geometric alignment despite uncertainty in perception, geometry, and con- trol. When this uncertainty causes unintended contact, the re- sulting contact provides local information that can guide correc- tive motion. Sampling-based Model Predictive Control (SMPC) is well suited to this setting because it optimizes through forward simulation without requiring gradients through contact dynamics. However, standard SMPC methods typically use generic proposal distributions that do not exploit observed contact to determine where to search next. We introduce ContactKernels, a contact-adaptive proposal kernel that uses geometry-conditioned wrench measurements to estimate contact location and local contact geometry. The estimated contact state directly adapts the proposal distribution: contact location biases the search toward corrective motions, while the contact normal shapes the sampling covariance. We evaluate ContactKernels with Predictive Sampling (PS) and Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control across multiple insertion geometries in simulation and on a real robot. In simulation, ContactKernels improves mean insertion success by over 50 % points across both controllers. On the real robot, it increases insertion success from 53.3 % to 90.0 % and reduces mean time to insertion by 33 %. These results show that contact information can improve sampling-based control not only as feedback, but also by directly determining where the controller searches
papers.tldr: ContactKernels is a contact-adaptive proposal kernel for sampling-based MPC that uses geometry-conditioned wrench measurements to estimate contact location and local geometry, steering the sampling distribution toward corrective motions and substantially improving contact-rich insertion success and speed in simulation and on a real robot.

detailed_reading.motivation: 接触丰富的插入任务在感知、几何和控制存在不确定性时容易产生非预期接触，而接触本身携带局部几何错配信息，可指导纠偏运动。采样型模型预测控制（SMPC）无需对接触动力学求梯度，适合此类任务，但标准方法通常使用通用提议分布，未利用已观测接触来决定下一步搜索方向，导致接触后的探索效率低。
detailed_reading.method: 作者将销孔插入建模为SMPC问题：状态为销的SE(3)位姿，控制为末端六维速度旋量，在规划时域内用M个控制结点经三次插值表示控制序列，采样K条候选轨迹并通过接触动力学前向仿真评估；代价包含末端到孔口的平移对齐、SO(3)测地旋转对齐以及仅在平移对齐低于阈值后激活的插入进度项，分别用Predictive Sampling选最小代价序列或用MPPI进行代价加权更新，且只执行首控制并经Operational Space Control映射到关节指令后重规划。ContactKernels从几何条件化力/力矩测量中估计P个候选接触点、表面法向和归一化权重，以接触位置偏置提议分布朝纠偏运动搜索，以接触法向塑造采样协方差，并用接触置信度缩放适应强度，从而把接触状态直接注入提议核而非仅作为反馈。
detailed_reading.result: 在多种插入几何的仿真中，ContactKernels使PS和MPPI两种控制器的平均插入成功率提升超过50个百分点；在真实机器人上，MPPI结合ContactKernels将插入成功率从53.3%提高到90.0%，并将平均插入时间缩短33%。这些对比表明，接触信息不仅可作为反馈，还能通过决定控制器搜索位置显著改善采样型控制。
detailed_reading.conclusion: ContactKernels通过接触自适应的提议核，将估计的接触位置和局部接触几何用于偏置搜索与塑形协方差，使SMPC在接触后更高效地探索纠偏动作。该方法在仿真和真实机器人上均验证有效，且无需学习接触到动作的映射或对接触动力学求导，为接触丰富操作提供了一种测试时自适应方案。
detailed_reading.key_details: 方法假设夹持固定、孔位已知，接触估计器基于力/力矩测量输出候选接触点、法向与置信权重；关键实现包括接触位置偏置、法向协方差、置信度缩放，以及代价权重、插入激活阈值、规划时域、控制结点数、采样数和协方差等超参。其优势是零阶优化避免接触梯度且无需额外策略训练，但效果依赖接触估计精度与参数调节，当前验证集中在销孔插入和固定夹持设定。最终执行首控制并滚动重规划，真实机器人实验验证了实时闭环可行性。

papers.title: Stress-Query and Temporal Reliability of Vision-Language Models as copilots in Autonomous UAV Navigation
papers.authors_text: Hiago Sodre, Sebastian Barcelona, Vincent Sandin, Pablo Moraes, Andre S. Kelbouscas, Ricardo B. Grando
papers.abstract: Integrating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) into autonomous UAV navigation enables high-level semantic reasoning but introduces critical temporal bottlenecks that can destabilize flight control. This paper presents a systematic benchmark that evaluates the operational trade-offs among model scale, hardware constraints, and flight reliability. By subjecting the system to extensive stress tests on both a high-performance workstation and a constrained integrated-graphics laptop, we isolate the kinetic impact of inference latency against reasoning accuracy. Our findings reveal a performance dichotomy: lightweight models struggle with structural hallucinations that break deterministic state machines, while heavyweight models induce trajectory overcorrections due to inference lag. We demonstrate that a mid-weight architecture strikes the optimal balance, successfully rehabilitating navigation in degraded environments without compromising real-time stability across different hardware profiles.
papers.tldr: This paper benchmarks vision-language models as asynchronous UAV navigation copilots under stress and shows that mid-weight architectures best balance inference latency and reasoning accuracy, avoiding lightweight hallucinations and heavyweight trajectory overcorrections across hardware profiles.

detailed_reading.motivation: 将视觉语言模型引入无人机自主导航可提供高层语义推理，但模型推理延迟会破坏实时控制回路，导致轨迹偏差甚至碰撞；现有研究缺乏对模型规模、硬件约束与飞行可靠性之间定量权衡的系统评测。本文旨在识别VLM作为无人机副驾驶时的时序可靠性边界，并回答多大模型规模能在语义恢复与实时稳定之间取得最优平衡。
detailed_reading.method: 论文构建PX4 Autopilot、ROS 2 Humble与Gazebo Harmonic的高保真SITL测试台，采用快慢解耦的混合FSM-VLM架构：30-50 Hz确定性有限状态机用OpenCV提取线条和门等快速视觉基元并经MAVROS发送速度设定点，异步VLM经Ollama在本地接收周期相机帧并仅输出预定义JSON模式。系统对格式错误和逻辑错误分别校验，失败输出被FSM丢弃，并在推理等待期触发自适应降速和延迟感知回溯。实验比较Moondream 1.8B、LLaVA-LLaMA3 8B与LLaMA 3.2 Vision 11B，在RTX 4070 Ti 12GB高性能工作站和RTX 4050 6GB受限笔记本上运行；以Mission 1为基线，将异步查询间隔从5 s到30 s分档，每条件重复5次，每模型配置共30次自主飞行，并记录推理延迟、最大轨迹误差、JSON格式稳定性和任务成功率，同时用TRB=e_max/v_UAV量化可恢复时间边界，室内走廊取e_max约2.5 m、v_UAV约0.5 m/s，得到TRB约5 s。
detailed_reading.result: 实验显示明显的性能二分：轻量Moondream在边缘端平均延迟约2.39 s、最大误差约0.75 m，但格式稳定性仅约16.5%，结构化幻觉会破坏确定性状态机；重型LLaMA 3.2 11B在云端延迟约3.31 s、格式稳定性100%、最大误差约0.80 m，但在边缘端延迟约31.4 s、最大误差约35.19 m，远超约5 s的TRB并引发轨迹过修正或碰撞。中量级LLaVA-LLaMA3 8B在云端延迟约3.28 s、格式稳定性约99.5%，在语义恢复与实时性之间表现最均衡；但边缘端约11.54 s的延迟和约14.56 m误差说明其部署仍受TRB约束。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 论文证明VLM用于无人机闭环导航时，时序延迟而非单纯语义精度是决定系统生存性的首要因素；过轻模型因结构化幻觉破坏FSM，过重模型因推理滞后造成轨迹过修正，中量级架构在可用算力下能兼顾语义恢复与实时稳定。作者据此提出以TRB为平台和场景相关的部署判据，要求推理延迟低于可恢复边界，并为不同硬件配置下的VLM规模选择提供经验蓝图。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键方法细节包括：以JSON模式作为VLM与FSM之间的严格结构契约，将失败分为格式错误和逻辑错误并直接丢弃无效输出；通过异步查询、自适应降速和延迟感知回溯缓解推理窗口内的位置漂移；用TRB=e_max/v_UAV把空间可恢复性与推理延迟联系起来，实验中TRB约5 s，因此边缘端11B的31 s延迟必然越界。评测覆盖Mission 1至多阶段任务及Full Run，查询间隔5-30 s、每条件5次重复，主要指标为平均延迟、最大误差、格式稳定性和成功率。局限在于TRB依赖具体平台和场景，e_max与速度近似常数，结果主要来自SITL仿真而非真实飞行，任务矩阵和硬件配置有限，且量化与VRAM瓶颈会显著影响边缘延迟。

papers.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk
papers.authors_text: Qianli Ma, Limengxi Yue, Shuyang Xu, Yanpei Shi, Hongrui Liu
papers.abstract:
Intelligent agent interactions in real-world web environments are commonly constrained by request budgets, time delays, anti-crawling restrictions, and operational failure risks. Strategies solely optimizing task success rates often exhibit unusable phenomena such as "high success but high cost" or "low risk but conservative failure." This paper proposes a constrained agentic reinforcement learning model for web agents, unifying page access, search requests, and external API calls into a unified long-term decision-making framework with associated costs. It simultaneously incorporates cost budget constraints and tail risk control into the optimization objective: constructing a multidimensional cost vector comprising cumulative request count, total latency, and failure penalties to achieve budget compliance via Lagrange dual updates, while employing a CVaR risk term to suppress excessive exploration of high-failure-probability paths, thereby achieving an adaptive balance among "completion rate, cost, and risk."
  Experiments were conducted across 30-70 site/page templates and 800-1,500 end-to-end web tasks, including information extraction, price comparison, form submission, and cross-page navigation. Interaction sequences spanned 20-120 steps with tool scales of 30-200. Performance was benchmarked against unconstrained RL, budget-constrained RL, and rule-based/scripted web agents, quantifying task completion rates, cost-per-success, failure rates, and policy stability.
  Results demonstrate that at equivalent completion rates, our method reduces C-PS by 22%-31% and lowers failure rates by 18%-26% under high failure penalties. Under fixed budgets, task completion rates increase by 10%-16%, highlighting the necessity and effectiveness of constraint modeling for practical web agent deployment.
papers.tldr: The paper proposes a constrained agentic reinforcement learning model for web agents that integrates multi-dimensional request, latency, and failure costs with Lagrangian budget enforcement and CVaR tail-risk control, achieving a better balance among task completion, cost, and failure risk and empirically reducing cost-per-success and failure rates while improving completion under fixed budgets.

detailed_reading.motivation: 真实Web环境中的智能体常受请求预算、响应延迟、反爬限制和操作失败风险约束，仅优化任务成功率的策略容易出现高成功但高成本或低风险但保守失败的两极问题。论文旨在把完成率、成本与风险纳入统一决策目标，使Web Agent能够在实际预算和失败惩罚下稳定部署。
detailed_reading.method: 将Web任务建模为带多维成本的约束马尔可夫决策过程，状态由页面DOM特征、历史动作嵌入和工具冷却向量组成，动作覆盖DOM操作、搜索请求、外部API调用与导航，成本向量包含累计请求数、总延迟和失败惩罚。用Lagrange对偶更新约束乘子以逼近请求数、延迟和失败成本预算，并引入CVaR尾部风险项及辅助变量η实现可微优化，形成奖励减去拉格朗日成本惩罚再减去风险惩罚的联合目标。策略网络采用参数共享双通道Actor-Critic，策略分支输出动作分布，价值分支估计成本加权Q值；训练中使用经验回放、Adam优化和软更新，推理时按约束策略选择动作并在预算与风险边界内完成长程交互。
detailed_reading.result: 在30—70个站点/页面模板、800—1500个端到端任务、20—120步交互和30—200个工具的设定下，与无约束RL、仅预算约束RL及规则/脚本Web Agent对比，所提方法在同等完成率下将每次成功成本C-PS降低22%—31%，在高失败惩罚下将失败率降低18%—26%。固定预算下任务完成率提升10%—16%；表中完成率由无约束的72.30%提升到仅预算约束的74.80%、预算加失败风险约束的77.10%和CVaR约束的80.50%，C-PS由0.45降至0.32，失败率由18.20%降至12.50%。这些结果说明多维成本与尾部风险约束能同时改善成本效率和风险控制，并保持策略稳定性。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 多成本与失败风险约束建模能够缓解传统RL在Web Agent高成本、高失败率任务中的不可部署问题，通过Lagrange预算控制和CVaR风险抑制实现完成率、资源成本与失败风险的自适应平衡。该框架在异构任务和页面模板上表现出较强泛化与稳定性，为真实Web场景的高维长程交互提供了约束感知的决策路径。局限在于稀疏奖励或超长路径任务下策略收敛较慢且风险估计存在偏差，未来可结合分层规划和动态风险调节改进。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括请求数、延迟和失败惩罚三类成本约束，训练设置给出请求上限b1=12、平均延迟上限b2=600ms、失败成本上限b3=0.3，而实验部分又报告35次请求、600ms平均延迟和7.0失败惩罚的上限，说明预算参数存在多组设定。CVaR使用风险置信水平约0.8—0.95、实验风险阈值α=0.1和0.2、风险抑制系数μ约0.1—1.0，成本与风险控制系数λ_c约0.1—1.5、β约0.1—1.0；状态维度配置为DOM特征128、历史动作嵌入64、工具冷却32，总状态维度120—320，折扣因子0.98，回放容量约10^5、批大小64、Adam学习率约3e-5、软更新系数0.005。损失由期望奖励、各成本约束的拉格朗日惩罚和CVaR风险项组成，每次交互采集请求数、响应延迟和失败标签以构造累计成本向量。局限是约束乘子和风险系数需调参，CVaR与拉格朗日耦合增加训练复杂度，且在稀疏奖励和超长路径上收敛与风险估计仍不稳定。

papers.title: When to Make a Decision: Task-Sufficient Active Perception for Mobile Manipulator Robots
papers.authors_text: Mariana da Silva Barros, Matthias Kerzel, Cornelius Weber, Stefan Wermter
papers.abstract: A robotic agent operating in an unknown environment must gather sufficient task-relevant information before acting. However, determining when the available information is sufficient remains a challenge. We propose a conceptual hybrid neuro-symbolic framework for task-sufficient active perception in unknown environments. After interpreting a requested task, the agent generates an initial plan and iteratively reevaluates it as new information becomes available. At each iteration, it can acquire a more informative viewpoint, inspect or manipulate candidate objects, ask the user for clarification, or perform the task. Neural perception modules update an object-centric belief state, while a symbolic decision layer determines whether the remaining uncertainty justifies further information gathering. The framework will be implemented on a mobile manipulator comprising a humanoid torso and a mobile base, with complementary evaluation in simulation. The proposed approach aims to enable robots to determine not only how to gather additional information, but also when further perception is no longer necessary.
papers.tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid neuro-symbolic framework that enables mobile manipulator robots to decide when task-relevant uncertainty is sufficiently resolved to act, by selecting among exploration, inspection, user clarification, and task execution in an uncertainty-aware decision loop.

detailed_reading.motivation: 机器人在未知且动态的环境中执行任务前，必须收集足够的任务相关信息，但现有方法常将规划、感知、探索和交互分离，导致机器人可能收集无关信息或信息不足，核心难题是判断当前知识何时对任务执行已经充分。
detailed_reading.method: 论文提出一个混合神经符号框架：用大语言模型将自然语言任务解释为结构化任务表示，用CNN或Transformer检测、语义分割及VLM视觉语言 grounding 更新以对象为中心的语义记忆信念状态；符号决策层结合神经感知不确定性、空间不确定性和任务级不确定性，在主动感知（基于Next-Best-View选择期望降低语义不确定性的视角）、对象检查或操作、向用户澄清、执行任务之间迭代选择，并用行为树组织决策与重规划。系统计划在NVIDIA Isaac Sim和由人形躯干与移动底座组成的移动操作机器人上实现，并用域适应进行仿真到现实迁移。
detailed_reading.result: 本文是概念性框架论文，尚未给出实际实验结果或可复现的定量对比；计划评估任务成功率、路径与动作计划、达到目标所需步数，以及探索、检查或澄清后神经感知不确定性如何变化，并考察机器人是否避免依据低置信度或歧义预测行动。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 该工作旨在让移动操作机器人不仅知道如何收集更多信息，还能判断进一步感知何时不再必要，从而以任务充分而非完整场景理解为目标，在遮挡、感知歧义和任务说明不完整等可复现场景中提升未知环境下的鲁棒性。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现点包括对象中心信念状态记录位置、语义类别、检测置信度、观测历史和视觉语言嵌入，任务充分性判据融合检测置信度、空间与任务级不确定性并设置执行阈值，主动感知以期望语义不确定性降低选择视角，决策采用符号行为树并复用ELMiRA的人机交互结构；任务覆盖物体搜索、取回和导航，仿真包含遮挡、相似物体和歧义指令。局限性是当前仅为概念与计划，缺少实证结果，阈值校准、异构信息收集动作的成本与风险比较、仿真到现实迁移及真实平台验证仍需后续完成。

papers.title: Learning Whole-Body Kinetic Coordination for Wheeled-Quadruped Long-Range Throwing
papers.authors_text: Qinglian Wu, Yidian Hu, Weiqi Fan, Yutian Zhang, Siyuan Ma, Jiaqi Zhai, Wei Dong, Li Xu
papers.abstract: Long-range throwing on unstructured terrain is a key capability for mobile robots in delivery and retrieval tasks, but it requires high release velocity, coordinated whole-body motion, and robustness to terrain-induced disturbances. We present a whole-body kinetic-coordination framework for a wheeled-quadruped manipulator that combines kinetic-chain arm modeling with SQP-based trajectory optimization and a reference-guided reinforcement learning policy for coordinated base motion. The manipulator is first reduced to a kinetic-chain model and optimized under kinematic and dynamic constraints to produce a high-speed throwing reference. On a stationary base, the optimized arm trajectory reaches a release speed of 12.75 m/s and a throwing distance of 16.68 m. When whole-body coordination is enabled, the system further increases the release speed to 16.64 m/s and the throwing distance to 28.25 m. We then integrate the mobility of the wheeled-quadruped platform and validate the complete policy through hardware experiments on flat ground, grass, slopes, and rough roads. The results show that kinetic-chain optimization and whole-body coordination together enable robust long-range throwing across diverse unstructured terrains.
papers.tldr: The paper presents a whole-body kinetic-coordination framework that combines kinetic-chain-based SQP arm trajectory optimization with reference-guided reinforcement learning for a wheeled-quadruped manipulator, enabling robust long-range throwing on unstructured terrain with up to 16.64 m/s release speed and 28.25 m distance when whole-body coordination is enabled.

detailed_reading.motivation: 轮式四足机械臂在非结构化地形上执行远程抛掷，对配送与取回任务很重要，但需要高释放速度、全身协调运动以及对地形扰动的鲁棒性。现有学习式运动控制多关注底盘移动，全身控制多面向一般操作，抛掷研究又常局限于固定基座或慢速移动基座，尚未充分解决地形扰动下机械臂反作用力与底盘稳定性的耦合问题。为此，作者希望将类人动能链的近端到远端能量传递与地形鲁棒的全身稳定控制统一起来。
detailed_reading.method: 方法分两阶段：先将机械臂简化为保留J2、J3、J5三个主动矢状关节的3-DOF动能链模型，用等效刚体组、耦合惯量项和动能Hessian推导惯性矩阵，并在近端关节高速、远端零力矩的近似下导出三个关节的正弦基函数形式。随后以基函数幅值、频率、相位、偏置和释放时刻为决策变量，用SQP最大化沿目标方向的加权末端释放速度，约束包括关节位置、速度、由完整动力学计算的力矩以及释放时刻位于有效抛掷区间。最后将优化得到的机械臂参考轨迹嵌入参考引导的全身强化学习策略，由策略协调轮式四足底盘并对机械臂施加小残差修正，同时利用基于历史信息的潜在表示适应地形，在仿真中联合训练后部署到硬件。
detailed_reading.result: 在固定基座下，优化后的机械臂轨迹达到12.75 m/s的释放速度和16.68 m的抛掷距离；启用全身协调后，释放速度提升到16.64 m/s，抛掷距离提升到28.25 m。作者进一步集成轮式四足平台 mobility，在平地、草地、斜坡和粗糙路面完成硬件实验，验证了完整策略的 run-and-throw 行为。结果表明动能链优化与全身协调结合能够显著扩展抛掷能力，并在多种非结构化地形上保持鲁棒。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 该工作表明，将动能链驱动的机械臂高速抛掷参考与参考引导的全身强化学习控制结合，可以在轮式四足平台上实现地形鲁棒的远程抛掷。其核心贡献在于统一处理机械臂反作用力、底盘稳定性和近端到远端能量传递，并通过多地形硬件实验证明该方法对非结构化环境具有实用性。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现上，动能链分析忽略重力并使用远端零力矩的被动响应近似，仅用于推导正弦基函数形式，实际轨迹可行性由完整机器人动力学和力矩约束在SQP中保证。优化目标中的正定权重矩阵用于强调期望抛掷方向上的释放速度分量，有效抛掷区间由正弦关节参考的零速度点定义。强化学习策略不直接替代优化轨迹，而是在优化参考附近学习底盘协调与机械臂残差修正，并用历史编码潜在表示增强地形适应。预览未给出完整RL超参数和训练规模，且方法依赖简化动能链建模与仿真到硬件的迁移验证，但其约束覆盖关节位置、速度、力矩和释放时刻，实验覆盖平地、草地、斜坡和粗糙路面。

papers.title: Context-Aware RGB-Thermal-Radar Obstacle Perception for Resource-Constrained ASVs
papers.authors_text: Pranav Kedia, Edwin Redhead, Heiko Hamann
papers.abstract: Reliable obstacle perception is challenging for small autonomous surface vessels (ASVs): reflections and glare confound visible-light cameras, vessel motion shifts the apparent waterline, and darkness removes the dominant sensing modality altogether. Rather than treating multimodal fusion as a static accuracy gain, we propose a context-aware architecture that combines RGB and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagery, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) mmWave radar, and inertial context. A bearing-sector interface provides the navigation controller with calibrated obstacle probabilities, radar ranges, and sensor status. It also distinguishes sensor dropout from a valid observation with no detected obstacle. Using new multimodal lake recordings, we deployed the pipeline in a 24-leg closed-loop pilot under uncontrolled lake conditions (16 day, 4 dusk, and 4 night; 351 m), including night legs in which RGB was unusable and the vessel drove on LWIR and radar evidence alone. On eight held-out low-light recordings, the calibrated fusion model achieved average precision (AP) 0.869 and expected calibration error 0.108, compared with AP 0.673 for rule-based fusion, 0.620 for gated fusion, and 0.903 for RGB alone. Our results expose a central tradeoff: RGB ranks best when usable, whereas fusion preserves a navigation input when RGB fails. This work is a step toward perception that remains usable and degrades predictably across multi-day ASV missions.
papers.tldr: This paper proposes a context-aware RGB–LWIR–mmWave radar fusion architecture with inertial context and a compact bearing-sector interface for small ASVs, showing through closed-loop lake trials that calibrated multimodal fusion preserves reliable obstacle perception when RGB fails, at the cost of slightly lower ranking accuracy than RGB alone when RGB is usable.

papers.title: Language-Forcing: Advancing Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Semantic Alignment of Whole-Body World Action Models
papers.authors_text: Yanjun Li, Jiarui Ye, Weiyu Guo, Zixiao He, Kangjie Ye, Dihan Wang, Yishuo Cheng, Zishang Xiang, Mingju Gao, Hao Tang
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict robot actions and future observations. However, their visual prediction objectives do not explicitly distinguish task-relevant transitions from incidental scene changes. For whole-body policies, this distinction matters because task progress depends on coordinated changes in body pose, contact, and object state. We introduce LANGUAGE-FORCING, a training strategy that uses language to emphasize task-relevant changes in the future visual representations of a whole-body WAM. Given paired current and ground- truth short-horizon future frames, a frozen vision-language model assesses task progress and predicts plausible subsequent state changes. We encode these descriptions with a frozen text encoder and align their embeddings with intermediate, action-conditioned future-visual features, complementing the original visual and action prediction objectives. All auxiliary components are used only during training, introducing no additional inference overhead. On HumanoidArena, LANGUAGE-FORCING achieves an average success rate of 79.17%, exceeding the strongest competing policy by 9.46 percentage points and the same WAM without language alignment by 10.77 percentage points. Across five real-world tasks, language alignment raises average success from 53.33% to 71.33% over the same WAM baseline.
papers.tldr: **TLDR:** LANGUAGE-FORCING is a training-only strategy that uses language to align task-relevant future state changes with the intermediate action-conditioned visual features of a whole-body World Action Model, improving humanoid loco-manipulation without adding inference overhead.

papers.title: PrismPlan: A Shared GPU Substrate for Motion Planning Across Paradigms
papers.authors_text: Hong Wu, ChaoXuan Liu, ShuJie Wang
papers.abstract: GPU acceleration has made motion planning one to two orders of magnitude faster, but it has not made the three paradigms---sampling, search, and optimization---comparable to one another: every GPU-accelerated planner is built around a single paradigm, so comparing across libraries also compares their collision checkers. All three, however, bottleneck on the same GPU primitive: batched collision detection and the batched forward kinematics beneath it. PrismPlan builds that primitive once, as a shared substrate of per-sphere collision--kinematics device code that every planner consumes. Because they all execute the same device code, the backend is held fixed by construction and the paradigms can be compared head-to-head. We run six planners over 1800 MotionBenchMaker problems on three robots (7--14 DoF, one a dual-arm whole-body composite) at an equal 2s budget. On the 7-DoF Panda, sampling (pRRTC) is the most reliable paradigm at 98%, while parallel search (wPA*SE) follows within four points at a 3-4 times$ lower median latency, and the local optimizers trail well behind when made to solve from scratch. On the 14-DoF dual-arm composite, sampling still solves about 90% of feasible problems, while no search or optimization planner clears a third of them. Our open-source code is available at https://github.com/XiaoyubotMotionTeam/PrismPlan.
papers.tldr: PrismPlan introduces a shared GPU substrate for batched collision detection and forward kinematics that lets sampling, search, and optimization planners run on identical device code for fair cross-paradigm comparison, revealing that sampling is most reliable—especially at high DoF—while search offers lower latency on 7-DoF arms and optimization lags when solving from scratch.

papers.title: MoDex: Towards Universal Multi-Object Dexterous Grasping
papers.authors_text: Jing Xiong, Jiale Xie, Haoqi Yuan, Chaoyi Xu, Zongqing Lu
papers.abstract: Multi-object grasping is a fundamental yet challenging problem, constrained by data collection costs, varying spatial layouts, and the need for broad generalization. To address these challenges, we propose MoDex, a data-efficient framework that provides the first unified solution for universal multi-object dexterous grasping across diverse spatial layouts. MoDex accomplishes this by formulating the task as a single-step decision problem of learning residual corrections to a reference trajectory, and introducing a spatially adaptive dual-strategy that performs single-shot grasping for proximal objects and sequential interaction for separated objects. Extensive evaluations show that MoDex significantly outperforms baselines in proximal configurations, achieving 61.24% success on unseen objects, and achieves high success rates in separated layouts. Further experiments demonstrate its generalization across robot embodiments, scalability and zero-shot sim-to-real deployment through a vision-based policy trained solely on simulation data. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/Aurora-Xiong/MoDex.
papers.tldr: MoDex is a data-efficient framework for universal multi-object dexterous grasping that learns single-step residual corrections to a reference trajectory and uses a spatially adaptive dual strategy—single-shot grasping for proximal objects and sequential interaction for separated objects—enabling strong generalization and zero-shot sim-to-real deployment.

papers.title: SAGE-CP: When Marginal Coverage Hides Route-Conditional Failures in Adaptive VLM Ensembles
papers.authors_text: Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer
papers.abstract: Adaptive VLM ensembles save computation by stopping early on easy images and escalating harder ones. Although a single conformal threshold can make the final predictor marginally valid, it can still fail severely along individual computational routes. We characterize this failure precisely: if a route has prevalence pi, marginal 1-alpha coverage allows its conditional coverage to fall to max{0, 1-alpha/pi}. To address this mismatch, we learn the router on development data, freeze all routing choices, and calibrate the returned score separately for early exits and escalated inputs. We call this pipeline SAGE-CP. Its calibration step applies Mondrian split conformal prediction to the operational groups created by the router. Under exchangeability, the resulting prediction sets achieve finite-sample coverage within each route. Across 10 benchmarks, 4 frozen VLMs, and 5 aligned splits, both global calibration and SAGE-CP achieve 0.900 marginal coverage at a 0.90 target, but their route behavior differs substantially. SAGE-CP raises mean worst-route coverage from 0.623 to 0.887 and reduces the mean route-coverage gap from 0.324 to 0.025, using the same routed scores and 1.177 source calls per image. The stronger guarantee increases the mean prediction-set size from 1.893 to 2.212; nevertheless, the sets remain smaller than those of the full ensemble (2.486) while requiring 70.6 percent fewer source calls. The route-level reliability persists across 6 fixed query fractions, while finer exit-depth groups demonstrate the need for additional calibration data on rare routes. Across 5 datasets, SAGE-CP also reduces measured batch-one latency by 58.8 to 63.4 percent and gross GPU energy by 55.7 to 57.5 percent relative to full inference. Thus, routing provides computational savings, while route-stratified calibration attaches coverage guarantees to the operational paths created by the router.
papers.tldr: SAGE-CP shows that marginal conformal coverage can mask severe route-specific failures in adaptive VLM ensembles, and fixes this by freezing the router and applying Mondrian split conformal calibration separately to each computational route, achieving stronger route-conditional coverage with modest set-size cost while retaining large latency and energy savings.

papers.title: AutoPruner: Agentic Depth Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors_text: Tao Lin, Yikeng Chen, Qiwei Liang, Zinan Xie, Zhengtu Liang, Renjing Xu
papers.abstract: Layer pruning reduces the size and inference cost of vision-language-action (VLA) models, but selecting a deployable configuration requires deciding both which layers to remove and how to recover task performance. These decisions depend on the model and task, and a failed trial can reflect either the deletion set or insufficient recovery. We present AutoPruner, an agent-driven framework that jointly searches pruning structures and recovery recipes through closed-loop experimentation. Offline layer interventions measure changes in action output to provide functional evidence. An LLM agent combines this evidence with evaluation history and retained diagnoses to propose deletion sets and recovery recipes within a search budget. Each proposal is executed and evaluated on the target tasks, and the resulting feedback guides the next experiment. Across OpenVLA-OFT, StarVLA, and FastWAM on four LIBERO suites, AutoPruner removes 16.7--87.5% of backbone layers while maintaining task success above 90%, with measured inference speedups of up to 2.50$\times$. Further analysis shows that functional probes identify action-sensitive layers despite high representation similarity, and that recovery can make previously failing structures viable.
papers.tldr: AutoPruner is an LLM-agent-driven framework that jointly searches layer-deletion sets and recovery recipes for vision-language-action models via closed-loop task feedback, enabling substantial depth pruning while maintaining over 90% task success and up to 2.50× inference speedups.

papers.title: InJePA: Intention-First Latent Planning with Coupled JEPA World Models for Visual Navigation
papers.authors_text: Siming Zhou, Bowen Ma, Ruiran Du, Pengcheng Zheng, Sheng Zheng, Dongshen Han, Zhijie Li, Wei Dong, Fan Mo, Chaoning Zhang
papers.abstract: Visual navigation requires goal directed planning informed by predictions of environment dynamics. Representative navigation world model methods propose complete action candidates before predicting consequences for selection or search updates. For each candidate, predictions primarily evaluate proposed actions rather than guide its stepwise construction. To this end, we propose InJepa, an intention first planning paradigm centered on latent states. A goal conditioned JEPA proposes latent intentions, and an action conditioned JEPA continually predicts future latent states. Both operate in a shared latent space to align their predictive representations. Within each candidate, predicted consequences feed into the next intention proposal and action inference, forming a closed loop of intention, action, and consequence. This extends the world model's role beyond evaluation to leading candidate construction through latent intentions. We evaluate InJepa through closed loop image goal navigation in Habitat MP3D. The results show effective multistep navigation through intention guided action generation and consequence feedback. Experiments across encoders further support applicability across visual representations. These findings support latent intentions as the central planning object and show that world models can directly guide plan construction through coordinated reasoning about intentions and consequences. Code is available at https://github.com/zhuxun132/InJepa.
papers.tldr: InJePA is an intention-first visual navigation framework that couples goal-conditioned and action-conditioned JEPA world models in a shared latent space, using predicted action consequences to iteratively guide latent intention generation and action inference in a closed loop.

papers.title: Transmission Error Compensation for Industrial Robots Using Fourier Series
papers.authors_text: Christian J. E. Bauer, Simon Nowinski, Valentin Kamm, Lukas Steinle, Armin Lechler, Alexander Verl
papers.abstract: Due to their low accuracy, industrial robots commonly require online teaching after the offline development of a robot program in simulation. The accuracy is limited by compliance and transmission errors in the robot joints. Transmission errors are defined as errors between the load-side angles of the gearboxes and the motor encoder angles. An approach to identify the transmission errors based on laser tracker measurements is presented. The developed velocity-dependent Fourier series model is integrated in a virtual commissioning software as a co-simulated functional mock-up unit. Additionally, it is used to compensate the transmission errors by correcting the setpoint from the computerized numerical control (CNC). The model identification and the compensation are experimentally evaluated with a Stäubli TX2-40 industrial robot. The model has a mean absolute error of 0.114 mrad, and the compensation improves the accuracy by 83.26 % for axis 2 and 49.21 % for axis 3.
papers.tldr: This paper identifies velocity-dependent industrial-robot transmission errors from laser tracker measurements, models them with a Fourier series for virtual commissioning and CNC setpoint feedforward compensation, and improves Stäubli TX2-40 accuracy by 83.26% on axis 2 and 49.21% on axis 3 with a 0.114 mrad mean absolute model error.

papers.title: UMI-WM: Interactive World Modeling for Bimanual Manipulation from Wrist Cameras
papers.authors_text: Jingxiang Guo, Haoyu Zhao, Xidong Zhang, Yuhang Zheng, Hao Wu, Chen Gao, Jianshu Zhou, Shuicheng Yan, Weihao Yuan
papers.abstract: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) pairs wrist-camera videos with camera trajectories and gripper openings, providing scalable, robot-free data for learning how bimanual actions change a shared scene. Existing interactive world models, however, typically rely on text or single-camera control and struggle to follow each arm's actions while maintaining consistency between the two wrist views. We introduce UMI-WM, an action-conditioned bimanual world model that jointly generates both wrist views from observation history, per-arm relative camera poses, and gripper widths, with cross-view consistency, action following, and visual fidelity. UMI-WM injects each arm's actions into its own wrist stream, while sparse hub tokens exchange scene information between the two streams. Camera-aware geometry conditioning and camera-guided noise further support per-view motion control and cross-view geometric exchange. We adapt the model for block-causal generation and distill the 30-step Teacher into a Student with four denoising steps. We train UMI-WM on self-collected open-world and in-studio UMI recordings combined with public manipulation data. To evaluate action following, we use an inverse dynamics model (IDM) to recover relative camera poses and gripper widths from generated videos, and introduce Bimanual Action Fidelity (BAF) to measure how closely these recovered actions match the conditioning actions. UMI-WM achieves the best results on all five reference-video fidelity metrics and the best or competitive performance on VBench and WorldArena. The Teacher and Student outperform all compared baselines in action following, while the four-step Student generates paired wrist videos 6.9 times faster than the Teacher.
papers.tldr: UMI-WM is an action-conditioned bimanual world model that jointly generates consistent left/right wrist-camera videos from UMI observations and per-arm camera/gripper actions, with a distilled four-step student that achieves strong action-following fidelity while generating paired views 6.9× faster than its teacher.

papers.title: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models
papers.authors_text: Simon A. Lee, Jiahang Hank Sha, Soomin Chung, Kai Akamatsu, Eran Halperin, Jeffrey N. Chiang
papers.abstract: We introduce a predictive world model for electronic health records (EHR) that represents patient histories as action conditioned latent trajectories. Rather than modeling clinical events solely through autoregressive token prediction, our framework explicitly separates patient states from observed clinical actions and learns their evolution through a state and action conditioned transition operator. At its core is a state dependent linearization predictor that propagates local changes in latent patient state, enabling time resolved prediction, multi step rollout, and action conditioned simulation. Empirically, we show that generated latent trajectories preserve downstream predictive signal, temporal structure, and subgroup level statistical relationships present in encoder derived representations. We further decode free running rollouts into the original clinical feature space and evaluate future clinical measurements against observed values using task matched forecasting baselines, demonstrating that the learned dynamics retain predictive information beyond latent space agreement. Across binary classification and time to event tasks, EHR WM achieves competitive, though task dependent, performance relative to substantially larger EHR foundation models while using a 30x smaller parameter footprint. Finally, perturbing observed action sequences produces corresponding changes in generated trajectories, demonstrating the action sensitivity of the learned dynamics. Together, these results support world modeling as a complementary framework for learning explicit, time indexed representations of patient evolution from longitudinal EHR.
papers.tldr: The paper introduces an action-conditioned latent world model for EHR data that separates patient states from clinical actions and learns a state-dependent linearized transition operator to forecast and simulate patient trajectories, achieving competitive downstream performance with a much smaller parameter footprint than large EHR foundation models.

papers.title: Announced Breaks Separate Conformal Reliability from Frequency Calibration
papers.authors_text: Karl Li
papers.abstract: An announced boundary reveals the partition before the first affected outcome, and a reset there serves one of two audits. The per-time audit reads conformal reliability, the expected distance of the threshold's coverage from nominal at miscoverage 0.1. The frequency audit reads frequency calibration, whether a closed window's error rate matched it. The reset rule, the post-boundary empirical quantile, attains the minimax per-time rate for independent scores. On bounded scores a recursion reset at the boundary attains a frequency gap of order one over the count when its floor adds a bounded total. At the 50th forecast after a large synthetic break, the reset rule's per-time gap stands below that of five adaptive methods, four from their authors' code, with every paired band below zero. After an electricity market reform, on 68 unseen scores, the band stands below zero against two, includes zero against two, adaptive conformal inference among them, and is a point at zero against one. After monetary policy decisions its pointwise band stands above zero against all five on 10 of the first 34 days. Of 9 announced boundaries one clears the smallest coverage difference its window detects, where every method's per-time gap at the 50th forecast exceeds the nominal miscoverage. Over the first 50 forecasts the reset recursion leads the frequency audit after every synthetic break.
papers.tldr: The paper shows that resetting conformal prediction at announced breakpoints separates per-time conformal reliability from frequency calibration, achieving minimax per-time coverage and strong frequency-calibration guarantees with empirical improvements over adaptive conformal methods after synthetic and real-world breaks.

papers.title: Lubricant Temperature Observer for Gearboxes in Industrial Robots
papers.authors_text: Christian J. E. Bauer, Markus Neher, Valentin Kamm, Lukas Steinle, Armin Lechler, Alexander Verl
papers.abstract: The position and path accuracy of industrial robots is strongly affected by temperature. In particular, temperature-dependent friction and altered hysteresis and transmission errors in the gearboxes are the main causes of these deviations. Since standard industrial robots lack temperature sensors, it is proposed to estimate the gearbox lubricant temperature using observer structures. It is planned to apply the proposed lubricant temperature observer to provide the input for temperature-dependent error compensation for gearboxes in industrial robots. First, a two-state heat transfer model describing the heat transfer from the lubricant through the gearbox housing to the environment is described and identified. It is integrated into a Luenberger observer and a Kalman filter with a correction of the lubricant temperature estimation based on measurements from a housing temperature sensor. Temperature measurements were performed in an experimental setup with a cycloidal gear filled with grease, which is common for industrial robots. Due to its changing viscosity and changing thermal conductivity at different shear rates, it shows a less uniform thermal behavior than gear-oil. For the validation measurements, the developed observers showed a mean absolute error of 1.3 K.
papers.tldr: This paper develops and validates Luenberger- and Kalman-filter-based observers that use a two-state heat transfer model and housing temperature measurements to estimate gearbox lubricant temperature in industrial robots, achieving a mean absolute error of 1.3 K for a grease-filled cycloidal drive.

papers.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding
papers.authors_text: Junchao Yang
papers.abstract: Adaptive speculative decoding changes the active batch size B and draft length d from one decode step to the next, whereas a CUDA Graph replays a fixed launch configuration. The resulting verification width M = B d forces serving systems to pre-capture many shapes, capture new ones on the serving path, or pad every step to the largest draft. We present PolyGraph, a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels that avoids this choice. PolyGraph captures one maximum-grid graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before each replay. Kernels skip tiles beyond that shape, while graph topology, allocations, layouts, pointers, and launch grids remain fixed; the update transfers only 28 bytes. On one NVIDIA H800, a trace-driven prototype with Qwen2.5-3B dimensions replaces 64 shape-specific graphs with one, matches the warmed baseline in observed step latency (17.7 vs. 17.8 ms P50), and reduces measured pre-serving graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms. Fixed-draft controls show that the benefit comes from avoiding padded payload: the P99 difference from MaxPad is negligible at zero padding waste but reaches an 18.7% reduction at 100% waste. Our evidence establishes a bounded work-shape mechanism for custom kernels, not a production serving system, and is limited to synthetic traces on one GPU.
papers.tldr: PolyGraph replaces many shape-specific CUDA graphs with one maximum-grid graph whose active speculative-decoding shape is written to a 28-byte GPU plan buffer before each replay, letting custom Triton kernels skip inactive tiles and match warmed-baseline latency while cutting pre-serving graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms.

papers.title: Adaptive Question Generation for Ambiguous Robot Instructions Based on Information Gain and Human Cognitive Characteristics
papers.authors_text: Ryo Terashima, Yuga Yano, Hakaru Tamukoh
papers.abstract: In this study, we propose an adaptive question generation mechanism that addresses uncertainty arising from ambiguous instructions. Natural-language instructions for service robots often contain ambiguities. In scenes with multiple similar objects, the robot must identify the target object by asking questions. However, existing question generation methods focus on probabilistic discrimination efficiency and do not sufficiently account for user ease of response. Asking questions without considering the user's ease of response may cause incorrect or uncertain answers. Such incorrect or uncertain answers lead to additional clarification turns and degraded dialogue efficiency. The proposed mechanism integrates probabilistic discrimination efficiency and human cognitive characteristics to generate questions that users can intuitively and easily answer. First, the proposed mechanism extracts visual attributes of candidate objects using a vision-language model (VLM). Next, the proposed mechanism computes the information gain (IG) of each attribute and selects the visual attribute (e.g., color, shape) that most reduces uncertainty in the candidate set. When multiple attributes have the same IG, the proposed mechanism applies a visual attribute filter based on cognitive characteristics to select the visual attribute that users can most intuitively perceive. The proposed mechanism then prompts the VLM with the selected attribute and the corresponding attribute values of each candidate object to generate a concise natural-language question. This process is repeated until the target object is uniquely identified. The proposed mechanism achieved a target identification success rate of 88.5% in the evaluation using a dataset of 120 scenes. Furthermore, the proposed mechanism received high ratings in subjective evaluations of response ease.
papers.tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive robot question-generation mechanism that combines information gain with human cognitive characteristics to ask concise, intuitive questions about ambiguous instructions, achieving an 88.5% target identification success rate and high subjective ease-of-response ratings.

papers.title: MicroSplat: Towards Automating 3D Small-Scale Reconstruction
papers.authors_text: Roman Mineyev, Robert Azarcon, Suvrat Jain, Chuizheng Kong, Shreyas Kousik
papers.abstract: Reconstructing sub-millimeter detail of small objects underpins tasks such as circuit-board defect detection, specimen digitization, and archiving. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) makes photorealistic reconstruction possible from posed images alone, but macro optics violate two conditions it depends on. The field of view (FOV) and the depth of field (DoF) shrink to millimeters, so viewpoint error can take a sample out of frame, and only a thin focal plane is sharp in frame. Existing automated macro-capture rigs handle the shallow DoF with per-view focus stacking, but typically rely on classical photogrammetry and offline, human-in-the-loop processing. We present MicroSplat, which generates a 3DGS using a low-cost consumer microscope on a manipulator arm. After a single up-front object-localization step, the system runs unattended. It performs calibration, plans collision-free viewpoints, captures and fuses a focal stack at each viewpoint, segments the object across all views, and optimizes a 3DGS model warm-started with the arm's own poses. We further compare against blur-aware 3DGS methods, which infer sharp scenes from defocused images, and find that measuring sharpness with a controlled focal sweep outperforms inferring it. We provide real and synthetic datasets (including robot and camera parameters) and the fitted 3DGS reconstructions.
papers.tldr: MicroSplat automates sub-millimeter 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction of small objects by pairing a robotic manipulator with a low-cost microscope and running an unattended capture-to-model pipeline that uses robot-pose initialization and per-view focus stacking, which outperforms blur-aware 3DGS methods.
